thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: cross-zone routing anomaly detected (us-west1 -> eu-west1). spike in 5xx for /v1/generate. Severity: P1. Affected: hosted API tenants. paging @jordan-oncall and netops. link: https://redwood/in/alerts/6661234567
jordan-oncall: ack — I'm on it, calling netops & infra. starting triage.
kim-netops: looking now. initial signal: steering-service returning stale assignment for a subset of us-west1 nodes — they're being routed to eu-west1 (ghost routes). counts: ~3% of traffic in the period.
amber-sre: adding myself. can you get the last policy diff id? also pulling healthchecks and kv-cache metrics.
kim-netops: diff=abcd1234, change removed fallback weighting and enabled sticky-pin TTL on route selector. deployed ~2026-03-15T10:12:05Z. suspect race where new pins overwrote active steering state during rollout.
devin-infra: propose revert to previous routing policy to stop new pins from being set. I'll stage a quick rollback to remove sticky-pin flag.
matt-sre: +1 to revert. preparing a canary patch to avoid broad blast. will monitor 5xx and latencies.
jordan-oncall: customer-impact: elevated 5xx and increased tail latency for cross-region requests, primarily affecting customers with EU/US traffic overlap. CS please notify affected accounts.
lucy-cs: drafting alert to top impacted tenants. ETA to send initial note ~5m. will include mitigation steps and timeline.
devin-infra: applying revert (canary):
```
kubectl -n routing apply -f /manifests/routing/policy-revert-canary.yaml
kubectl -n routing rollout status deploy/steering-service-canary --timeout=120s
```
matt-sre: canary shows drop in 5xx on ~20% of traffic. rolling revert to remaining hosts now.
kim-netops: note: DNS caches still hold old pin assignments; TTLs were 300s on many resolvers. even after revert some clients will continue to hit eu-west1 for a short window. coordinating cache flush and lower TTL.
amber-sre: reading health logs — KV cache eviction took a few cycles but lookups stabilized after the rollback. metrics: error rate back to baseline ~10m after full revert.
jordan-oncall: mitigation steps completed: policy revert, TTL reduction, cache flush requests sent to CDN/DNS teams. drafting timeline for postmortem.
lucy-cs: initial customer notices sent. AMs are queued for follow-ups. 
kim-netops: issued TTL override: pin-ttl=60 for affected selector and triggered CDN edge purge for known customers.
matt-sre: telemetry: 5xx decreased to baseline, tail latency normalized. marking incident as mitigated.
amber-sre: capturing notes for postmortem: root cause candidate = rollout introduced sticky-pin TTL without compatibility check with in-flight steering state -> race leading to transient misassignments. next actions: tighter rollout guards + canary policy checker + automated TTL sync.
jordan-oncall: switching to incident wrap and handoff. assigning postmortem owner @amber-sre. Great work team :thumbsup: 
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — recovered. start_time: 2026-03-15T10:41:00Z; end_time: 2026-03-15T10:58:42Z. links: runbook: https://redwood/in/runbooks/routing-ghost-route, logs: https://redwood/in/logs/6661234567, postmortem-draft: https://redwood/in/pm/6661234567-draft
